swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about protests against the Vietnam War.
swap.text: A symbolic form of protesting against the war involved burning these pieces of paper, which are issued to those registered in Selective Service.

question.leadin: Some conspiracy theorists claim that a gunman involved in this event stood on a grassy knoll, either in addition to or instead of a gunman in the Texas School Book Depository.
question.text: Name this November 22nd, 1963 event in which Texas governor John Connolly was wounded.
question.answerHtml: assassination of John F. Kennedy (accept equivalents for "assassination;" accept "JFK" for "Kennedy;" prompt on "assassination of Kennedy" alone)
question.clue: Police officer J.D. Tippit was killed shortly after this event, and both James Tague and Governor Connally were also injured in it.

swap.text: One of the largest riots in United States history occurred in New York in 1863 when this system was instituted, and it also was a motivation behind many student riots during the Vietnam War before this system was discontinued in 1973.

question.leadin: Name some things about the contentious nomination of Robert Bork to the Supreme Court.
question.text: Within an hour of the nomination announcement, this long-serving senator from Massachusetts took to the Senate Floor to denounce it. He never secured the Democratic nomination for the presidency as a result of an incident at Chappaquiddick Creek.
question.clue: This man stuttered that his "behaviour was inexplicable" when Roger Mudd asked him about chatting with a race-winning sailor the day after a supposedly traumatic event.

swap.text: Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein, journalists for this newspaper, investigated the Watergate scandal. Under Katharine Graham, this newspaper published the Pentagon papers after another newspaper was barred from doing so.
swap.answerHtml: Washington Post [accept WaPo; prompt on the Post] (The other newspaper was The New York Times.)
swap.clue: Under the editorship of Ben Bradlee, this publication published a series of documents detailing the US's involvement in Southeast Asia for four presidential administrations.

question.text: This vice president was not able to take power immediately after the shooting because he was on a plane. This successor to Reagan served one term before losing to Bill Clinton in the 1992 presidential election.
question.answerHtml: George H.W. Bush [or George Herbert Walker Bush; accept Bush 41 or George Bush Senior or Bush 1 or Bush the Elder or other names indicating the older Bush; prompt on Bush or George Bush; do NOT accept or prompt on “George W. Bush” or “Shrub” or “Dubya”]
question.clue: This president attacked his opponent for being "soft on crime" in the Willie Horton advertisement.

swap.text: McCarthy and Cohn were supported by this long-time director of the FBI in their efforts to root out homosexuals. This man also founded COINTELPRO to harass civil rights leaders like Martin Luther King, Jr.
swap.clue: An anonymous letter sent on this man's orders tried to convince Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. to commit suicide.

question.leadin: Identify these British folks who rebelled against Catholic Church doctrine.
question.text: This group, started by Gerrard Winstanley in 1649, was an offshoot of the Levelers and argued for radical Christian communitarianism and the cultivation of neglected land.
question.clue: Led early on by William Everard, the philosophy of this group was put forth in The New Law of Righteousness, the primary text by its major leader Gerrard Winstanley.

swap.leadin: Name these people who served as the U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations.
swap.text: The cofounder of the Zapata Petroleum Company, this future president served as U.N. Ambassador before becoming director of the CIA in 1976.
swap.answerHtml: George Herbert Walker Bush [prompt on George Bush; accept Bush the elder or anything that distinguishes him from his son]
swap.clue: This man lost a tennis match to Emperor Akihito hours before vomiting on the lap of the Japanese Prime Minister.

question.leadin: Answer the following about senators from Idaho.
question.text: Frank Church led the Church Committee, which exposed this CIA program. Ken Kesey and Allen Ginsberg were two subjects of this series of Cold War mind control experiments involving the administration of LSD.

swap.leadin: Jerry Rubin pulled stunts such as dressing as Santa Claus and blowing bubblegum bubbles when summoned by this group.

swap.clue: The "Hollywood Ten" were blacklisted for refusing to testify in front of this group, whose members included Jerry Voorhis and Richard Nixon.

question.leadin: Justice Potter Stewart, who coined the phrase "I know it when I see it" about this kind of material, was asked by a clerk whether he had ever, in fact, seen it, to which he responded "just once, off the coast of Algeria."
question.text: Name this type of material, defined in a 1973 case as material lacking "serious literary, artistic, political, or scientific value."
question.clue: The average person's application of "contemporary community standards" is one of the three prongs of the Miller test for whether this word is applicable.

swap.text: Nicknamed the "Junk Bond King," this Wall Street trader headed the high-yield bond department at Drexel Burnham Lambert until he was sold out by Ivan Boesky.
